To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytonuclear Zonula occluded‐1 (ZO1) pool is a new regulator of CXCL8 expression in tumor cells via the nuclear factor‐κB (NF‐κB) pathway.
the tight junction protein ZO‐1 is able to regulate the expression of the proangiogenic cytokine IL‐8 via the NF‐kB signaling pathway.
ZO‐ 1, a scaffolding protein involved in tight junctions, is a novel regulator of CXCL8 transcription via the p65 subunit of NF- κB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ZO‐ 1, a scaffolding protein of the tight junctions, in the regulation of tumor angiogenesis.
the regulation of CXCL‐8/IL‐1 expression in lung and mammary tumor cells.
the role of the ZO‐ 1 shuttle from the junction to the cytoplasm and nucleus of tumor cells in the regulation of the expression of IL‐8 and in the establishment of the proangiogenic microenvironment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZO‐ 1 is a new regulator of angiogenesis via the NF‐kappa B pathway and the CXCL8/ IL‐8 axis.
ZO‐ 1 regulates CXCL‐8/IL‐ 8 expression via the nuclear factor kappa B (NF‐κB) signaling pathway and its 95 subunit, which modulate the transcription of IL- 8.
ZO-1 regulates CXCL-8 expression via NF-kB signaling, and its p65 component, which subsequently modulate the transcription of IL-8.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ZO‐ 1 is a new regulator of CXCL8, a proinvasive chemokine, via the NF‐kB signaling pathway and its P65 subunit.
ZO-1 is involved in the regulation of CXCL-8 expression in tumor cells and that this regulation is mediated by a NF-kappaB pathway.
ZO‐ 1, a tight junction protein, regulates the expression of CXCL8, a pro‐invasive chemokine, via the NF‐kB pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ZO‐ 1, which was initially described as a tight junction protein, can regulate the expression of the proinvasive chemokine CXCL8.
ZO‐ 1, a scaffolding protein of the tight junctions, can regulate the transcription of CXCL8 (IL‐8) via NF‐κB.
